title: Difference of Number of Distinct Values on Diagonals
summary: Given a 2D grid of size m x n, compute a new grid where each cell's value is the absolute difference between the number of distinct values on the diagonal to the left and above the cell, and the number of distinct values on the diagonal to the right and below the cell, excluding the cell itself.
statement: Given a 2D grid of size m x n, compute a new grid where each cell's value is the absolute difference between the number of distinct values on the diagonal to the left and above the cell, and the number of distinct values on the diagonal to the right and below the cell, excluding the cell itself. The diagonals run from the top-left to the bottom-right direction. Return the resulting grid.
constraints: For each cell, inspect its top-left diagonal before the cell and its bottom-right diagonal after the cell.
Count distinct values on each side, excluding the cell itself.
Return their absolute count difference at every matrix position.
hints: For each output cell, use two sets.
Walk repeatedly up-left from the preceding diagonal cell, and down-right from the following diagonal cell.
Store the absolute difference of the two set sizes.
The walks enumerate exactly the two open diagonal rays, while sets collapse repeats as required by distinct counting.
editorial: The walks enumerate exactly the two open diagonal rays, while sets collapse repeats as required by distinct counting.

tests.explanation: The distinct diagonal counts yield rows [1,1,0], [1,0,1], and [0,1,1].
Opposite corner cells see one diagonal value while the other two see none, producing [[1,0],[0,1]].
